content: 1. Infliximab and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. 2. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of live varicella virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also elevate the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 3. Vedolizumab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration of vedolizumab with TNF blockers should be avoided due to the potential for increased infection risk. 4. Infliximab decreases the efficacy of the yellow fever vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also heighten the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 5. Infliximab reduces the effects of the live zoster vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 6. Infliximab increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Belatacept and infliximab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at doses exceeding physiologic levels), may diminish the immune response to the cholera vaccine. 9. Infliximab decreases the efficacy of the dengue vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Immunosuppressive therapies (e.g., radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, corticosteroids at supraphysiologic doses) may reduce the immune response to the dengue vaccine. 10. Infliximab and denosumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems are at higher risk for serious infections. 11. Infliximab increases immunosuppressive effects, while echinacea decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Efgartigimod alfa reduces the level or effect of infliximab through receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of efgartigimod with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider discontinuing efgartigimod if long-term use of such medications is essential. 13. Efgartigimod/hyaluronidase reduces the level or effect of infliximab through receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of efgartigimod with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider discontinuing efgartigimod if long-term use of such medications is essential. 14. Infliximab increases the effects of fingolimod through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Concomitant therapy is expected to increase the risk of immunosuppression. Exercise caution when switching patients from long-acting therapies with immune effects. 15. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as the antibody response might be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence has been restored. 16. Hydroxyurea and infliximab may increase the risk of immunosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ifosfamide and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the quadrivalent recombinant influenza virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. The immune response to the vaccine may be diminished in immunocompromised individuals. 19. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the trivalent recombinant influenza virus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. The immune response to the vaccine may be diminished in immunocompromised individuals. 20. Infliximab and isavuconazonium sulfate both decrease immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lomustine and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems are at higher risk for serious infections. 22. Infliximab increases immunosuppressive effects, while maitake decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Mechlorethamine and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems are at higher risk for serious infections. 24. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the meningococcal group B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Individuals with altered immune competence may have reduced immune responses to the vaccine. 25. Infliximab and mercaptopurine both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Infliximab and ocrelizumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of ocrelizumab with immunomodulators is expected to increase the risk of immunosuppression. 27. Infliximab and ocrelizumab/hyaluronidase both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of ocrelizumab with immunomodulators is expected to increase the risk of immunosuppression. 28. Ofatumumab SC and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider the risk of additive immune system effects when co-administering immunosuppressive therapies. When switching from therapies with immune effects, consider the duration and mechanism of action of these therapies when initiating ofatumumab SC. 29. Infliximab and olaparib both increase pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents, including DNA-damaging agents, may potentiate and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. 30. Ozanimod and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immunosuppressive therapies may increase the risk of additive immune effects during therapy and in the weeks following administration. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, consider the half-life and mode of action of these drugs to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 31. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the inactivated poliovirus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as the antibody response might be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence has been restored. 32. Ponesimod and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised if co-administered due to additive immunosuppressive effects during such therapy and in the weeks following administration. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, consider the half-life and mode of action of these drugs to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 33. Rozanolixizumab reduces the level or effect of infliximab through receptor binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of rozanolixizumab with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness, and consider discontinuing rozanolixizumab if long-term use of such medications is essential. 34. Siponimod and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Caution is advised if co-administered due to additive immunosuppressive effects during such therapy and in the weeks following administration. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, consider the half-life and mode of action of these drugs to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 35. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of sipuleucel-T due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 36. Trastuzumab and infliximab both increase toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. The incidence of neutropenia or febrile neutropenia was increased when trastuzumab was co-administered with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. 37. Trastuzumab deruxtecan and infliximab both increase toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. The incidence of neutropenia or febrile neutropenia was increased when trastuzumab was co-administered with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. 38. Ublituximab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Owing to potential additive immunosuppressive effects, consider the duration of effect and mechanism of action of these therapies if co-administered. 39. Infliximab and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec may potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Closely monitor these medications and consider alternative medications in case of potential drug interactions. 40. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the recombinant zoster vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine. 41. Cat’s claw and infliximab may increase each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, but possible additive immunosuppression may occur. 42. Abatacept and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of serious infection. This combination is contraindicated. 43. Adalimumab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Alefacept and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Anakinra and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the anthrax vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 47. Antithymocyte globulin (equine) and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Antithymocyte globulin (rabbit) and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Infliximab increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them. The interaction's effect is unclear, so caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Infliximab and axicabtagene ciloleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 51. Azathioprine and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Baricitinib and infliximab both increase toxicity through immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Baricitinib is not recommended in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs, or potent immunosuppressives. 53. Basiliximab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 54. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the live BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 55. Belatacept and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Infliximab and brexucabtagene autoleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 57. Canakinumab and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 58. Cat’s claw and infliximab may increase each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, but possible additive immunosuppression may occur. 59. Infliximab and certolizumab pegol both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid this combination due to an increased risk of serious infection. 60. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at doses exceeding physiologic levels), may diminish the immune response to the cholera vaccine. 61. Infliximab and ciltacabtagene autoleucel both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 62. Cyclosporine and infliximab both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 63. Infliximab reduces the efficacy of the dengue vaccine due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. Immunosuppressive therapies (e.g., radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, corticosteroids at supraphysiologic doses) may reduce the immune response to the dengue vaccine.
